claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To get started, I need to gather some information about your circumstances.

Let me begin with my first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'd like to know if I'm eligible for Child Benefit. 

I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 16 years old, there are some specific rules that apply to his situation.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he in school, college, university, or an apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school and isn't doing any courses or anything like that right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex left education or training, there may still be a possibility for Child Benefit to continue.

**Has Alex registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He just finished school and hasn't signed up for anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask one more important question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in paid work, and if so, how many hours per week is he working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just at home with me right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, I can now make my determination:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

Unfortunately, you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: While Child Benefit can normally continue for children aged 16-19 if they remain in approved education or training, Alex does not meet this condition. He is also not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, which would have allowed eligibility to continue for 20 weeks following his departure from education.

**Possible next steps:**

If Alex were to enter approved education or training, or if he registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you may become eligible for Child Benefit again. If that happens, please feel free to reach out again or contact HMRC directly for guidance on restarting your claim.

Additionally, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Alex has not registered with either of these services. Therefore, you do not qualify for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.
